title: Design Review Loop QA
eyebrow: QA · #592: reviewer, acceptance run, parked questions and deviations ledger

short.lead: The design review loop is built and its acceptance run passes all nine criteria on your Windows PC (round 2). Please check that the results read right, then reply with a pass or say what failed.
short.hint: Tap a row to see what was checked and how.
items: All nine criteria pass on your PC

Round 2 ran docs/qa/design-review-loop/run_acceptance.py on your Windows machine, with one output file per search text in the round-2/ folder next to it. Every criterion from C1 to C9 shows PASS, and the STATUS line reads pass. Round 1 (6 passed, 3 failed) is recorded in round-1.md in the same folder.

Your first PC run failed everything. The design_loop checks crashed because a test stood in for gh (the GitHub command-line tool) with a shell script, which Windows cannot run. Also, a plan page saved with Windows line endings looked changed after review, so its review stamp no longer matched. Both are fixed, and the passing round 2 run covers them.

Running scripts/acceptance.py stamp wrote acceptance-stamp.json after the round passed, and acceptance.py check reports that stamp as current. ledger.py check reports 9 criteria and 2 rounds, and says the ledger is valid.

Open docs/qa/design-review-loop/round-2.md and read the nine PASS lines. Then open one output file, such as docs/qa/design-review-loop/round-2/c6-1.txt, and confirm it ends with the passing checks for the combined approval (a design approval and a build plan approval given in one message).
Follow the to-do steps in the Wrap-up section.

changes: The close-facts tests no longer need a shell script.
The tests stood in for gh (the GitHub command-line tool) with a #!/bin/sh shell script, which Windows cannot run. So the design_loop checks crashed and reported no results.
Those tests now use a Python stand-in for gh, and their six checks pass on Windows.
A page saved with Windows line endings keeps its review stamp.

The review stamp is a hash of the page text as read. A page saved with Windows line endings (CRLF) therefore hashed differently from the reviewed version and looked out of date. That made the check refuse the plan half of a combined approval.
The hash now treats Windows line endings (CRLF) and Unix line endings (LF) as the same.

unverified: Nine checks still fail in a full verify.py run on your Windows PC: three in the guard (branch by cwd, audit entries, a delete under the temp folder), two page checks, three waitfor checks and one node check. The same nine failed before the line-ending fix, so neither fix caused them. They were not investigated, and whether they also fail on a clean main was not checked.
The full verify.py run after both fixes shows 1572 of 1581 checks passing; the nine above are the only failures.
The deviation check works by matching phrases, and it has not been seen firing in a live session.
No test covers the two-round cap, re-review of changed picks, or the page-mode and plan-mode checks run separately.
Round 1 was written into ledger form afterwards from report.md, not from a fresh run
